# Fieldnote Analytics: 18-month cash budget, Jan 2026 – Jun 2027

**Bottom line:** John's plan runs out of cash in **March 2027**, about 9 months before his mid-2027 raise. Under board policy, the latest raise must close in **August 2026**, so fundraising has to start by **March 2026**.

## 1. Monthly cash budget

**Column formulas**
- **Opening MRR** = prior opening MRR + new MRR − 2% × prior opening MRR. New MRR is $6,000 through Jun 2026 and $9,000 from Jul 2026. January opens at $52,000.
- **Revenue** = opening MRR, collected the same month.
- **Gross profit** = 78% × revenue.
- **Payroll (burdened)** = 1.22 × (current $105,000/mo + hires' monthly cash pay). Hires start Mar (2 engineers, $27,500/mo), Apr (AE, $13,333/mo) and Jul (CSM, $7,500/mo).
- **Other opex** = $38,000 + $1,500 × number of new hires on payroll.
- **Data license** = $144,000 in each January, otherwise $0.
- **Net burn** = payroll + other opex + data license − gross profit.
- **Ending cash** = prior ending cash − net burn. It starts at $2,400,000.

| Month | Opening MRR | Revenue | Gross profit | Payroll | Other opex | Data license | Net burn | Ending cash |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan-26 | 52,000 | 52,000 | 40,560 | 128,100 | 38,000 | 144,000 | 269,540 | 2,130,460 |
| Feb-26 | 56,960 | 56,960 | 44,429 | 128,100 | 38,000 | 0 | 121,671 | 2,008,789 |
| Mar-26 | 61,821 | 61,821 | 48,220 | 161,650 | 41,000 | 0 | 154,430 | 1,854,359 |
| Apr-26 | 66,584 | 66,584 | 51,936 | 177,917 | 42,500 | 0 | 168,481 | 1,685,878 |
| May-26 | 71,253 | 71,253 | 55,577 | 177,917 | 42,500 | 0 | 164,840 | 1,521,038 |
| Jun-26 | 75,828 | 75,828 | 59,146 | 177,917 | 42,500 | 0 | 161,271 | 1,359,767 |
| Jul-26 | 80,311 | 80,311 | 62,643 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 168,424 | 1,191,343 |
| Aug-26 | 87,705 | 87,705 | 68,410 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 162,657 | 1,028,686 |
| Sep-26 | 94,951 | 94,951 | 74,062 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 157,005 | 871,681 |
| Oct-26 | 102,052 | 102,052 | 79,600 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 151,467 | 720,214 |
| Nov-26 | 109,011 | 109,011 | 85,028 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 146,039 | 574,175 |
| Dec-26 | 115,831 | 115,831 | 90,348 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 140,719 | 433,456 |
| Jan-27 | 122,514 | 122,514 | 95,561 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 144,000 | 279,506 | 153,950 |
| Feb-27 | 129,064 | 129,064 | 100,670 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 130,397 | 23,553 |
| **Mar-27** | 135,482 | 135,482 | 105,676 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 125,391 | **(101,838)** |
| Apr-27 | 141,773 | 141,773 | 110,583 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 120,484 | (222,322) |
| May-27 | 147,937 | 147,937 | 115,391 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 115,676 | (337,998) |
| Jun-27 | 153,978 | 153,978 | 120,103 | 187,067 | 44,000 | 0 | 110,964 | (448,962) |

Figures are computed on unrounded MRR, then rounded. Negative cash after March 2027 is the cumulative funding gap.

**Assumptions I added:**
- Hires cost a full month in their start month.
- The AE's variable pay is paid at target, monthly, and carries the 22% burden.
- The license is separate from the 78% gross margin (which covers hosting and data processing) and renews at the same price in January 2027.
- There are no raises, recruiting fees or interest, and churn is unaffected by the CS hire.

## 2. Where John's estimate goes wrong

John's burn is $105,000 + $12,000 + $38,000 − $52,000 = $103,000/mo.

| Error | Effect on monthly burn |
|---|---|
| Payroll is unburdened: $105,000 should be $128,100 with the 22% burden | **+$23,100** |
| Revenue is treated as cash profit. Hosting and data processing cost 22% of revenue ($11,440 on $52,000) | **+$11,440** |
| The four hires are omitted. At full run-rate they cost $58,967 payroll plus $6,000 opex | **+$64,967** from July 2026 |
| Revenue is held flat at $52,000. MRR actually grows, so July gross profit is $62,643 vs $40,560 | **−$22,083** by July 2026 |
| The license is smoothed at $12,000/mo, but $144,000 is paid each January. Annual cost is the same, but cash timing differs | **+$132,000** in January, **−$12,000** in other months |

**Reconciliation:**
- January: $103,000 + $23,100 + $11,440 + $132,000 = **$269,540**.
- July: $103,000 + $23,100 + $11,440 + $64,967 − $22,083 − $12,000 = **$168,424**.

John's 23-month runway is $2.4M ÷ $103k. The real runway is about 14 months. His "afford all four hires" conclusion is wrong because his burn never included them.

## 3. Cash-out and fundraising dates

- **Cash runs out in March 2027.** Ending cash in February 2027 is $23,553, less than one month of burn.
- **Board policy test** (ending cash ÷ that month's net burn, which must be at least 6.0×):

| Month | Ending cash | Net burn | Coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Jul-26 | $1,191,343 | $168,424 | 7.1× |
| Aug-26 | $1,028,686 | $162,657 | 6.3× |
| Sep-26 | $871,681 | $157,005 | 5.5× |

- Coverage breaches 6× in September 2026, so the **raise must close by August 2026**.
- Raises take about 5 months, so the **latest start is March 2026**. That leaves zero slack, so I want to start in February.
- John's mid-2027 raise would begin after the money is gone.

## 4. Recommendation and alternatives

**Recommendation: keep the hiring plan, but start the raise now and make the July CS hire conditional.**
- Target kickoff in February 2026 and a close by July–August 2026.
- Size the raise at **at least $1.5M**. The cumulative gap to June 2027 is $449k, and holding 6 months of burn (about $666k) needs roughly $1.1M more. This cushion also covers slippage.
- Hire the CSM in July only if a term sheet is in hand or MRR is on plan (about $80k opening MRR in July). Otherwise defer them.
- Do not cut the AE: it is the growth lever behind the story investors will fund.

**Cost of each hire per month (burdened, plus $1,500 opex):** each engineer $18,275; AE $17,767; CSM $10,650.

**Scenario A: delay the CSM from July 2026 to January 2027.**
- It saves $10,650 × 6 = $63,900.
- End-February 2027 cash becomes about $87,000.
- Cash still runs out in **March 2027**.
- The raise deadline moves from September to about October 2026 coverage, so only a few weeks of slack.
- It is a useful lever but does not fix the problem.

**Scenario B: no AE, new MRR stays at $6,000.**
- It saves $17,767/mo from April.
- Lost gross profit from slower MRR offsets this by about March 2027. Cumulative net savings through February 2027 are about $132k.
- Cash runs out in **April 2027**, only one month later.
- Coverage falls below 6× in October rather than September, so the raise deadline moves by one month.
- June 2027 opening MRR would be about $124k vs $154k, so you lose roughly $30k of MRR for a one-month extension.

**Conclusion:** hiring choices move the cash-out date by a month or two. Only a raise changes the outcome. A cut in hires is a fallback if the raise slips, with the CSM first and then one engineer (about $18k/mo).
